letter.subject: Concerns about cookie and tracking practices on beazley.com
letter.body:
Dear Data Protection Officer,

I am writing to raise concerns identified during an automated, passive audit of https://beazley.com on 2026-11-08 04:14 UTC. Using a fresh browser, the audit visited https://www.beazley.com/en-gb/, https://www.beazley.com/en-us/ and https://www.beazley.com/en-sg/, clicked the cookie banner’s “Reject All” option, and recorded what cookies and requests were still sent. Your privacy and cookies statement at https://www.beazley.com/en-sg/privacy-and-cookies-statements was also reviewed.

The points I ask you to explain are:

1. Our review suggests there may be a discrepancy between the policy wording and the observed tracking. The policy states: “We use this information to compile statistical data on the use of our websites, but the information obtained is used on an anonymous, aggregated basis and you cannot be identified from this.” However, the audit observed Google advertising and analytics cookies containing what looked like unique identifiers, as well as Hotjar session-replay requests. Our review suggests this appears inconsistent with the statement that visitors cannot be identified from the information.

2. Three Google cookies were observed as already set before any choice was made on the cookie banner: _ga, _ga_MEJKRCK4D2 and _gcl_au. These appeared to hold unique identifiers.

3. After “Reject All” was clicked, 8 requests to googletagmanager.com were still observed.

4. After “Reject All” was clicked, 4 requests to hotjar.com were still observed.

5. The privacy policy appears to name 4 companies, but Hotjar was observed and no mention of Hotjar was found. I appreciate the policy may describe some recipients by category rather than by name.

Please would you:

1. Explain each of the points above.
2. Confirm which cookies and trackers you consider strictly necessary or otherwise exempt, and why.
3. Stop any non-essential cookies or tracking that are set or activated without consent.
4. Reply within one month.

If this matter cannot be resolved satisfactorily, it may be raised with the Information Commissioner’s Office.

Yours faithfully,
Joshua Baker
